paper_title: A Comprehensive Survey on Multimodal RAG: All Combinations of Modalities as Input and Output
outline_pattern: Taxonomy-driven followed by a process-oriented workflow analysis

sections.title: Introduction
sections.description: Introduces the evolution of Large Language Models (LLMs) to Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) and the necessity of Multimodal RAG (MM-RAG) to mitigate hallucinations. It highlights the limitations of existing surveys, presents the paper's unique contribution (covering all modality combinations), and outlines the paper's structure.

sections.title: Problem Formulation
sections.description: Provides the mathematical definition of the MM-RAG framework. It defines the three core components: the Knowledge Base (D), the Retriever (R), and the Generator (G), and formulates the optimization objective of minimizing the difference between generated output and ground truth.

sections.title: Taxonomy
sections.description: Presents a comprehensive taxonomy matrix based on 54 possible input-output modality combinations. It analyzes existing work within these combinations and identifies unexplored areas.

subsections.title: Input
subsections.description: Analyzes encoders and processing methods for various input modalities used to query the knowledge base.

subsections.title: Text
subsections.description: Discusses text as the basic modality for retrieval, using models like BERT and T5.

subsections.title: Image
subsections.description: Covers image inputs using encoders like ViT, ResNet, and Vision-Language Models (CLIP, BLIP) for alignment.

subsections.title: Audio
subsections.description: Examines audio inputs using models like Wav2vec, HuBERT, and CLAP.

subsections.title: Video
subsections.description: Discusses video inputs, utilizing Large Video Language Models or converting video to text/images for processing.

subsections.title: Code
subsections.description: Reviews code as a modality, using specialized encoders like CodeT5 and GraphCodeBERT.

subsections.title: Structured Data
subsections.description: Discusses knowledge graphs and tables as inputs for tasks like KBQA and Table QA.

subsections.title: Others
subsections.description: Briefly touches on other modalities like time-series data forecasting.

subsections.title: Output
subsections.description: Analyzes the generation capabilities for different output modalities based on retrieved information.

subsections.title: Text
subsections.description: Covers text generation from multimodal inputs (e.g., image captioning, VQA) using LLMs and MLLMs.

subsections.title: Image
subsections.description: Discusses image generation using GANs, diffusion models, and VLMs augmented by retrieval.

subsections.title: Audio
subsections.description: Reviews audio generation (TTS, music) using spectral generation or large audio models.

subsections.title: Video
subsections.description: Discusses the nascent field of RAG-based video generation using diffusion models.

subsections.title: 3D data
subsections.description: Covers text-to-3D generation using retrieved 3D assets or motion samples.

subsections.title: Code
subsections.description: Examines code generation and completion using retrieved documentation and snippets.

subsections.title: Insights from the Taxonomy
subsections.description: Summarizes the findings from the taxonomy matrix, highlighting empty cells as opportunities for future research and summarizing common models for core components.

sections.title: Workflow
sections.description: Deconstructs the MM-RAG system into four essential operational stages: Pre-retrieval, Retrieval, Augmentation, and Generation.

subsections.title: Pre-Retrieval
subsections.description: Focuses on preparing the data and the query before the actual search occurs.

subsections.title: Knowledge Base Preparation
subsections.description: Details data preprocessing, chunking, and organization methods (Uni-modal Embedding, Pair-wise Storage, Unified Embedding, Graph Construction).

subsections.title: Query Preparation
subsections.description: Discusses techniques to refine inputs: Query Expansion, Rewriting, Transformation, Dropout, and Multi-Query strategies.

subsections.title: Retrieval
subsections.description: Analyzes the core retrieval mechanisms used to fetch relevant documents.

subsections.title: Retriever
subsections.description: Compares Sparse Retrievers (BM25), Dense Retrievers (CLIP, DPR), and other specialized retrievers.

subsections.title: Retrieval Strategy
subsections.description: Reviews strategies like Hybrid Retrieval and Hierarchical Retrieval.

subsections.title: Retrieval Timing
subsections.description: Discusses when retrieval occurs: Single, Iterative, or Adaptive Retrieval.

subsections.title: Augmentation
subsections.description: Describes how retrieved data is processed before being fed to the generator.

subsections.title: Context Reranking
subsections.description: Re-scoring retrieved documents to improve precision.

subsections.title: Context Selection
subsections.description: Filtering irrelevant or redundant information.

subsections.title: Context Compression
subsections.description: Reducing dimensionality or size of embeddings to fit context windows.

subsections.title: Noise Injection
subsections.description: Adding noise during training to improve model robustness.

subsections.title: Context Fusion
subsections.description: Methods to integrate query and documents: Fusion by Concatenation (FiE, FiD) and Fusion by Latent Aggregation.

subsections.title: Generation
subsections.description: Details the generator architecture (Modality Encoder, Projectors, LLM Backbone, Modality Generator).

subsections.title: Enhancement Approaches
subsections.description: Discusses Prompt Engineering and MLLM Fine-tuning to improve generation quality.

sections.title: Training Strategies
sections.description: Categorizes approaches for training MM-RAG systems based on parameter updates.

subsections.title: Parameter-Frozen Strategies
subsections.description: Discusses using off-the-shelf models without fine-tuning to reduce costs.

subsections.title: Parameter-Trainable Strategies
subsections.description: Covers methods that update model parameters for better alignment.

subsections.title: Modular Training
subsections.description: Independent optimization of components (Retriever, Generator, Extra Layers).

subsections.title: End-to-end Training
subsections.description: Joint training of retriever and generator for holistic optimization.

sections.title: Evaluation and Benchmarks
sections.description: Discusses metrics and methods for assessing MM-RAG performance.

subsections.title: Evaluation of the Retriever
subsections.description: Focuses on Retrieval Relevance and Retrieval Quality metrics.

sections.title: Applications
sections.description: Discusses various applications of MM-RAG (inferred from Introduction roadmap).

sections.title: Future Directions
sections.description: Explores future research opportunities in the field (inferred from Introduction roadmap).

structural_insights.organization_logic: The paper follows a classic engineering survey structure: Definition -> Taxonomy (What) -> Workflow (How) -> Training (Build) -> Evaluation (Measure). This logical flow allows readers to first understand the landscape before diving into technical implementation details.
structural_insights.transition_strategy: The paper uses the Taxonomy Matrix (Table 1) as a central pivot. It first defines the matrix to categorize existing literature, then uses the specific modality combinations identified in the matrix to structure the detailed technical discussions in the subsequent sections.
structural_insights.depth_analysis: The paper shows significant depth in the 'Workflow' section (Section 4), breaking it down into four distinct stages with multiple sub-strategies. This contrasts with the 'Taxonomy' section which is broad but shallower, serving as an index. The inclusion of 'Pre-retrieval' and 'Augmentation' adds necessary granularity often missed in simpler RAG surveys.
key_strengths: Comprehensive Taxonomy Matrix covering 54 input-output combinations.
Clear separation of the RAG workflow into four distinct, actionable stages.
Detailed breakdown of specific encoders and generators for every modality type.
Structured comparison of training strategies (Frozen vs. Trainable).
